tutAskMega: This is Mega mode: some numbers span two lines. Want to see how it’s played?
tutAskColor: This is Colour mode: every block has a colour. Want to see how it’s played?
tutC1: A number has the colour of its block. The palette lists the colours and how many cells of each are still open.
tutC2: The second row is one red block of 5. Choose red, then fill the row.
tutC3: Different colours may touch. The middle column is a red 2 and then a green 2. Fill the red cells, switch to green, and fill the rest.
tutC4: Two blocks of the same colour still need an empty cell between them. Finish the picture.
tutCEnd: That is Colour. A game’s own colour puzzles are marked 🎨. A colour version of a black-and-white picture is marked ✨.
colorFromGameHelp: This is one of the game’s own colour puzzles.
colorByMomoHelp: Made by MomoGram from the colour picture of the game; its solutions were checked.
colorHelp: Colour mode: puzzles where every block has a colour. Blocks of the same colour need a gap between them, blocks of different colours may touch. Pick a colour below the board.
noColor: None of your games has colour puzzles yet.
tagline: All your nonograms in one place. Careful, it eats time.
noGameData: MomoGram ships without any game data. Everything it reads from your games stays on this device.
dailyHelp: 15 fresh puzzles every day, 5 per difficulty
randomHelp: A random puzzle from your library
tutAsk: New to nonograms (or to MomoGram)? A short tutorial shows how it works.
tut1: The numbers are the filled blocks in that row or column. An empty cell separates two blocks. Let us solve this picture.
tut2: The top row says 5, and the row is five cells long, so every cell is filled. Draw across it.
tut3: The third row and the middle column also say 5. Fill both.
tut4: Separate numbers are separate blocks. 1 1 1 in five cells fits only as fill, empty, fill, empty, fill. The middle fill is already there. Add the other two.
tut5: The bottom row says 1, and that cell is filled. The other cells are empty. Switch to ✕ and mark those four.
tut6: A number turns grey once its block is complete. Finish the picture. Switch back to fill when you need to.
tutEnd: That is all of it. Easy points out mistakes. Normal and Hard leave them to you, and they award higher medals.
tutM1: A Mega number belongs to two lines at once. It is one connected shape that reaches into both.
tutM2: Rows 2 and 3 are a pair. The framed 2 is the Mega shape. The small numbers are ordinary blocks: the upper one stays in the upper row, the lower one in the lower row.
tutM3: Fill the leftmost cell of row 2 and of row 3. That is the Mega 2, one cell in each row, touching.
tutM4: Finish the picture. A Mega shape may bend. Its cells still have to touch.
tutMEnd: That is Mega. Turn it on from the home screen and any picture can be played this way.

pointsExplain: Points: everything you have solved, each puzzle counted once with its best medal (platinum counts most).
wrongAsk: Show your mistakes? This puzzle then only gives a bronze medal (and counts like Easy for PixELO).
parHelp: Par: the time a 1000 PixELO player needs. Faster raises your PixELO and gives a speed bonus.

createHelp: Pick game files you own (Game Boy, Super Famicom, DS, DSiWare, Arduboy, decrypted 3DS; loose, zipped, 7z or rar). Switch games are folders: pick the decrypted RomFS folder with "Add a game folder", or add a zip of it. MomoGram reads the puzzles once and turns every game into a pack: keep the pack files and you never need the games again. Packs (.momopack, or older .json and .zip files) go through the same button.

p_spotHelp: A puzzle halfway through: find a cell you can be sure of now, and fill it or cross it out.
p_spotTask: Find a cell that is certain now: fill it or cross it out.
pNoPuzzles: Your games have no puzzles that fit this game yet.

p_lineHelp: One row or column is marked. Looking only at its numbers, some of its cells must be filled and some must stay empty: find them all.
p_lineTask: Look only at the numbers of the marked line: {n} of its cells must already be filled or crossed out. Find them.
p_memoryHelp: You see the picture for 3 seconds, then solve it from memory (and the numbers).
tA1: Slide a long block to the left edge, then to the right edge. Fill every cell it covers both times.
tA2: With several numbers, pack them tight from the left and again from the right. Fill a cell only when the same number covers it both times.
tA3: A filled cell on the edge belongs to the first number. Finish that block, then mark the next cell with ✕.
tA4: A ✕ works like an edge. The filled cell beside it starts the block. Finish the block and mark every cell the block cannot reach.
tA5: Two filled cells of one block must be joined. Fill the gap between them, and mark the cells that are too far away for that block.
tA6: A gap between ✕ marks that is too short for any remaining number is empty. Mark it, then place the numbers in what is left.
tA7: This block can only be the 2, so it is finished. Mark both sides of it, and everything after the last number.
tA8: If filling one cell would make the numbers impossible, that cell is a ✕. One cell in this line works that way. Find it.
tA9: When the numbers and one empty cell between each of them fill the line exactly, there is only one arrangement. Fill it.
tAEnd: Those are the line techniques. Use them on rows and columns together. Practice, then One line, trains them.
tMA1: A Mega number always uses both lines of its pair. A Mega 2 is two cells, one above the other. Find them.
tMA2: A Mega 3 is an L across both lines. Fill the cells that every possible L here has to use.
tMA3: A Mega number needs a free cell in both lines. Where only one line is free, mark it empty.
tMA4: An ordinary number in a Mega pair stays on its own line and does not touch the other line. Mark the cells beside it, including across, and the rest of its line.
tMAEnd: A Mega number covers both lines, stays connected, and never touches the ordinary numbers of its pair.
tCA1: Different colours may touch. The same colour needs a gap. Both lines here fit in only one way. Fill them.
tCA2: The overlap trick works per colour. Fill a cell only when the same colour covers it from both ends.
tCA3: Only the middle column contains red, so this row’s red cell has to be there. The rest of the row is empty.
tCAEnd: Same-coloured blocks need a gap. The crossing line tells you which colours can sit in a cell.
